messages:
irene_auditor: Hi team — auditor request: for SOC2 CC6/CC7 we need a crosswalk that maps recent incidents (last 12 months) to the evidence artifacts we can provide (logs, runbooks, signed incident timelines, KMS key access records). Please include S3 export paths, SIEM alert IDs, CloudTrail query snippets, and any RBAC change PR links. Can someone assemble a short manifest by EOD?

alex_dev: Working on it. I can start by listing incidents and where artifacts live. Will attach a minimal example mapping first.

alex_dev: Example mapping format (short):
- incident_id: INC-2025-042
- date: 2025-02-14
- summary: transient mem leak -> degraded serving on prod-us
- artifacts: [s3://redwood-evidence/incidents/INC-2025-042/timeline.pdf, s3://redwood-evidence/incidents/INC-2025-042/logs.tar.gz]
- cloudtrail_query: "eventName:\"StartInstances\" AND resources.type:Instance"
- siem_alert: SIEM-98321
- kms_evidence: s3://redwood-evidence/incidents/INC-2025-042/kms-access.json (CMK ID arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111122223333:key/abcd-ef01)

maria_security: Nice. Two quick notes: 1) KMS access artifacts are the CloudTrail lookup_events query output and KMS GetKeyRotationStatus/GenerateDataKey logs — I usually export them to JSON and include the key_id. 2) For RBAC changes, include the GitHub PR link + kubectl apply diff snippet so auditors can see who approved.

maria_security: Example CloudTrail query we used for the KMS access extraction:
```
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=ResourceName,AttributeValue=arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111122223333:key/abcd-ef01 --start-time 2025-01-01T00:00:00Z --end-time 2025-12-31T23:59:59Z
```
This returns all KMS related events for that CMK.

sam_eng: For RBAC PR evidence, here's the actual kubectl snippet included in the PR for the scoped fix (we changed a ClusterRoleBinding to RoleBinding in the data-plane namespace):
```
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: svc-data-plane-readonly
  namespace: data-plane-prod
subjects:
- kind: User
  name: service-account:data-processing@redwood
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: data-plane-reader
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
```
PR link: https://github.com/redwood/infrastructure/pull/4287 (approved by @maria_security and @ops_oncall)

ops_oncall: FYI we also captured the audit logs from Kubernetes API server for that change, exported to s3://redwood-audit/k8s-audit/2025/02/14/cluster-audit.json.gz. That contains the user and timestamp to satisfy change control evidence.

alex_dev: Putting together the manifest CSV now. Will include columns: incident_id, period, control_ref, artifact_paths (comma-separated), siem_ids, cloudtrail_snippet, pr_links, approvers, notes. Attaching first two rows inline so auditors can preview: 
INC-2025-042,2025-02-14,CC6;CC7,"s3://redwood-evidence/incidents/INC-2025-042/timeline.pdf;s3://redwood-evidence/incidents/INC-2025-042/logs.tar.gz;s3://redwood-audit/k8s-audit/2025/02/14/cluster-audit.json.gz",SIEM-98321,"aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=ResourceName,AttributeValue=arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111122223333:key/abcd-ef01 --start-time 2025-02-13T00:00:00Z --end-time 2025-02-15T23:59:59Z",https://github.com/redwood/infrastructure/pull/4287,"maria_security;ops_oncall","notes: key rotation check included"
INC-2025-121,2025-05-09,CC6,"s3://redwood-evidence/incidents/INC-2025-121/postmortem.pdf;s3://redwood-evidence/incidents/INC-2025-121/siem_exports/alerts.ndjson",SIEM-100222,"siem query: index=alerts host=prod-us | incident_id=INC-2025-121",https://github.com/redwood/services/pull/5010,"alex_dev","notes: demonstration of automated rollback"

maria_security: A couple of auditor Qs I've seen before — they often want: evidence of detection (SIEM export + rule ID), evidence of response (runbook timeline with signatures), and evidence of preservation (immutable S3 snapshot + checksum). For checksums we put SHA256 file alongside each artifact, e.g., s3://redwood-evidence/incidents/INC-2025-042/timeline.pdf.sha256.

irene_auditor: This is perfect. Two followups: 1) Can you add a short explanation for any artifacts that are KMS-wrapped (how key access was logged and who had decrypt rights at the time)? 2) For RBAC changes, provide a short table mapping change -> enforcement (e.g., why ClusterRoleBinding->RoleBinding reduced blast radius).

alex_dev: Yes. For KMS-wrapped artifacts we include a companion JSON with the CloudTrail events showing kms:Decrypt or kms:GenerateDataKey calls and the principal. Example KMS access JSON path: s3://redwood-evidence/incidents/INC-2025-042/kms-access.json (contains eventTime, eventName, awsRegion, userIdentity.arn). We'll add a one-line explanation in the manifest notes.

sam_eng: For RBAC mapping: we'll add a short rationale field in the manifest: "Change reduced scope from cluster-wide to single namespace, limited subject to service-account, removed wildcard subjects." Also add a query to show active RoleBindings now: `kubectl get rolebinding -n data-plane-prod -o yaml | grep -A2 svc-data-plane-readonly`

audit-bot: Automated snapshot created: evidence-snapshot-INC-2025-042-2056789033.tar.gz uploaded to s3://redwood-evidence/snapshots/2056789033/ (manifest attached). Hash: sha256:9f2c3b1a...

maria_security: I'll prepare a short control mapping doc that states which artifact types satisfy which SOC2 tests (detection -> SIEM exports; change control -> PR + Approvals + k8s-audit; key management -> CloudTrail/KMS API logs + rotation policy). Will link it in the manifest.

alex_dev: Final ask — ops_oncall, can you confirm retention proof for the CloudTrail bucket and S3 versioning state? We need a policy link for auditors.

ops_oncall: Confirmed. CloudTrail logs are stored in s3://redwood-cloudtrail-logs/ with lifecycle policy retain 2 years, and Versioning=MULTI for redwood-evidence buckets. Policy doc: https://internal.redwood.com/policies/log-retention#cloudtrail. I'll attach a signed statement.

irene_auditor: Thank you. If you can export the manifest CSV + control mapping doc + one sample incident snapshot (not full set) to the auditor portal by EOD, we can review and request any gaps. This thread is great — keep comments short and put links in the manifest so we can iterate. :thumbsup:
